StorytellerDef.label: The Long Road
StorytellerDef.description:
More of the story happens out in the region. Raids come to the gate at the classic pace, and the region brings more: letters asking for help, favours called in, camps on the land, missions and quests, travellers on the road. Ambushes and chance meetings happen more to the colony's caravans than at its walls.

For a game of journeys and the region map.

It shifts the odds this way but shuts nothing out: every kind of event can still come.

StorytellerDef.label: Neighbours
StorytellerDef.description:
Most of the story comes from the peoples around the colony. Raids come at the classic pace, and most come from a people with a reason: one the colony wronged, or an old enemy. Peoples call in their favours, ask the colony to join their quarrels, and write and visit more often, and a people the colony has helped is more likely to send fighters when the colony is attacked.

For a game of diplomacy, debts and old grudges.

It shifts the odds this way but shuts nothing out: every kind of event can still come.

StorytellerDef.label: The Turning Year
StorytellerDef.description:
The seasons shape the year. Spring is quiet, though sickness comes with the thaw. Summer is the growing season, with heat waves and blight. Autumn, once the harvest is in, brings trade and camps. Winter is hard, with cold snaps and the hardest raids late in the season. Every year follows the same pattern with different events in it, so the colony can plan for its seasons. Over a year, threats and sickness come about as often as at the classic pace.

For a game of fields, stores and the colony's calendar.

It shifts the odds this way but shuts nothing out: every kind of event can still come.

StorytellerDef.label: What You Sow
StorytellerDef.description:
What happens depends on the colony's deeds, as the peoples remember them. Raids come at the classic pace whatever the colony does, but its deeds decide who comes. Cruelty brings raiders with a grievance, and fewer traders, visitors and friends in a fight (a quarter of them still come); kindness brings traders and visitors, and friends to the gate in a fight. None of this is announced: the world simply responds, and its peoples remember for longer.

For a game where how the colony treats others matters.

It shifts the odds this way but shuts nothing out: every kind of event can still come.

StorytellerDef.label: Old Powers
StorytellerDef.description:
More of the story is strange and unexplained. Raids come nearly at the classic pace, and stranger threats make up the rest: psychic drones, maddened herds, things in the earth, and the void's own threats where Anomaly's content is on. Omens and strange nights come often, with eclipses and auroras. Pilgrims and seers travel more, Rimfolk's events about the land and the sky come more often, and the old powers' own strange happenings come about twice as often (a seer at the end of a season, a stone that hums, a night sky in other colours, an animal that speaks, pale wolves under the full moon). News from the region turns to strange skies.

For a game of omens and the unknown.

It shifts the odds this way but shuts nothing out: every kind of event can still come.

StorytellerDef.label: Lean Years
StorytellerDef.description:
Scarcity is the main danger, more than raiders. Raids come at the classic pace, while blights, cold snaps, heat waves and storms come often, traders are few and camps are rarer. News from the region is of famine, drought and hard winters. The colony has to keep everyone fed and warm through hard years.

For a game of fields, stores and keeping everyone fed.

It shifts the odds this way but shuts nothing out: every kind of event can still come.

StorytellerDef.label: Rise and Fall
StorytellerDef.description:
The story runs in arcs of two years: one year of growth, then one year of trouble. In the first year raids come a little less often than at the classic pace, and traders, visitors and camps come in plenty. Early in the second year news comes from the region of a great trouble (a war among the peoples, a plague, a famine, a hard winter or a darkness in the sky), and about a season later the trouble itself arrives: the war's raids, the plague's sickness, the famine's blights, the winter's cold. The second year ends with a quiet time of rebuilding, with friends at hand, and then the next arc begins. Over the two years, threats and sickness come about as often as at the classic pace.

For a game of long stories with an ending to each.

It shifts the odds this way but shuts nothing out: every kind of event can still come.

StorytellerDef.label: Crossroads
StorytellerDef.description:
The colony is a market on a road through the land. Traders come about twice as often, orbital traders too, along with visitors, travellers and merchants' camps, and there are more debts and favours between the colony and its neighbours. Raids come at the classic pace, larger as the colony's wealth grows, and some come from rivals with a grudge. News from the region is of fairs, trade, roads and tolls.

For a game of trade and wealth.

It shifts the odds this way but shuts nothing out: every kind of event can still come.

StorytellerDef.label: Open Gate
StorytellerDef.description:
More people come to join the colony. Wanderers ask to join, refugees and escape pods arrive, wild people wander in, and more visitors come. Guests more often ask to stay a while, and some of them stay for good. Rimfolk's events in which someone may join come more often. How many come still follows the storyteller's sense of how big the colony should be. Raids and everything else come as in the base game.

For a game of a growing colony.

It shifts the odds this way but shuts nothing out: every kind of event can still come.

StorytellerDef.label: Home and Hearth
StorytellerDef.description:
The story stays at home with the colonists. Their personal stories start about twice as often, their pasts catch up with them more often, and Rimfolk's challenges and wagers come more often. Feasts, fairs and games come more often, and the steward thinks of holding a feast with guests sooner. Raids and everything else come as in the base game.

For a game about the colonists' own lives.

It shifts the odds this way but shuts nothing out: every kind of event can still come.

StorytellerDef.label: The Wilds
StorytellerDef.description:
Animals and the land are the story. Herds pass through more often, animals wander in and join, thrumbos and other rare beasts pass by, and the land turns up more finds, such as ambrosia and wild crops. Rimfolk's events of animals and great beasts, and of the land and the sky, come more often, and so do the colonists' moments with animals. News from the region turns to herds and beasts. Predators, maddened animals, raids and everything else come as in the base game.

For a game of hunting, taming and the land.

It shifts the odds this way but shuts nothing out: every kind of event can still come.

StorytellerDef.label: Windfalls
StorytellerDef.description:
The colony finds more. Cargo pods, ship chunks and meteorites fall more often, and peoples send gifts more often. Treasure maps, buried caches, sealed crates and old vaults turn up, and the region offers more stashes, ruins and wrecks to explore. News from the region turns to wrecks and opened vaults. Raids come as in the base game and still grow with the colony's wealth.

For a game of scavenging and exploring.

It shifts the odds this way but shuts nothing out: every kind of event can still come.

StorytellerDef.label: Sellswords
StorytellerDef.description:
The colony is asked to fight for others. Allies call it to arms more often, bandit camps to clear and outlaws with a price on their heads are offered more often, and travelling champions come more often to challenge the colony's best. Sellsword companies look for work in the region more often and come to the gate to be hired. Raids on the colony come as in the base game.

For a game of fighting for pay and for friends.

It shifts the odds this way but shuts nothing out: every kind of event can still come.

StorytellerDef.label: Feast Days
StorytellerDef.description:
Festivals fill the calendar. Rimfolk's feasts, fairs and games come more often, and the steward thinks of holding a feast with guests sooner. Performers and storytellers visit more often: players, fiddlers, spirit-singers and fortune tellers. News from the region turns to great fairs, moots of the peoples, bumper harvests and seasons of songs. Raids and everything else come as in the base game.

For a game of feasts and good company.

It shifts the odds this way but shuts nothing out: every kind of event can still come.
